message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in Monopoly.

I'm p1 with $233 and four unmortgaged properties. p2 has a dark blue monopoly but mortgaged both greens. I just paid $18 rent to p4.

p3 has a brown monopoly with hotels and no yellows. p4 owns light blue hotels and several yellows, but lacks Atlantic Avenue. I already hold Marvin Gardens, so I am blocking p4's yellow monopoly.

I also block p4's pink monopoly with my St. Charles and States properties.

Atlantic Avenue is unowned. The bank has 32 houses and 7 hotels.

My total liquidity is $768. That covers one light blue hotel if I mortgage now. I should not unmortgage New York Avenue.

Unmortgaging New York Avenue would leave me with only $123. That is too risky against a light blue hotel costing $550–$600. I will not unmortgage it.

I will not mortgage now. I have no urgent cash need.

I am considering trading. p3 might accept a lower price for Marvin Gardens, though they previously rejected $400 and may want at least $350. p2 is also a possible target, but I do not want his mortgaged greens.

I will not trade with p2. He has $239 and could build dark blue houses if I give him cash. I do not need his mortgaged greens because p3 already blocks that set.

Trading with p4 is too risky. He wants my yellow blocker and pink properties, which I must keep.

I am now looking for a trade that gives me cash without giving up those blockers.

Water Works is not a blocker, but giving it to p3 would let them collect 10x dice rent from both utilities. That is too risky.

I cannot buy the unowned Atlantic Avenue through trading.

I will hold my current holdings and end the turn.

Light blue hotels are the biggest threat at $550–$600 each. Brown hotels are less dangerous at $250–$450. Dark blue is only $70–$100 without houses.

The orange set is the best long-term development target, but it requires roughly $1010 to build three houses. That is far beyond my current cash of $233. I will not spend money on development now.

I considered trading Marvin Gardens to p2, but p2 does not own yellows and would still need Ventnor, Kentucky, Penn, and Atlantic to complete a yellow monopoly. That would not remove p4's blocker.

I should warn p2 not to sell Indiana or North Carolina to p3. That would complete p3's green monopoly. I might buy those greens myself to block p3.

Acquiring Indiana and North Carolina mortgaged would block p3 without paying unmortgage fees. But p2 needs cash to build dark blue houses, and a Boardwalk hotel would cost $2000. That would kill everyone including me.

I cannot afford to pay p2 more than about $100 for Indiana and North Carolina. That would still leave him with enough cash to build dark blue houses.

A property-for-property swap is not viable because I have no valuable pieces to offer in exchange.

I will not publicly warn p3, since p2 is actively soliciting offers and p3 has the cash to complete a green monopoly.

I am now calculating the exact rent and house costs for a green monopoly. Pacific Avenue, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania each cost $200 per house. With $697 in cash, p3 can build one house on each property. I also realized Indiana is red, not green.

p4 owns Pennsylvania Avenue, a green property. The green set is split three ways across p3, p2, and p4. No player can complete a green monopoly without buying from another owner.

I am now checking which color groups are split across players. The red set is already divided among p3, p2, and p4. I also noticed that yellows are only three properties long, so p4 already holds three of them.
